propositions: Path.rglob traversal in _remove_readonly_run_snapshots caches directory entries and raises FileNotFoundError on Python 3.11 when a cached child directory (specifically .tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock.d) vanishes during descent due to concurrent LockHandle.release() calls

Python 3.11 pathlib consults live os.name during Path construction in test teardown, selecting WindowsPath when monkeypatched to 'nt' by test bodies, raising NotImplementedError before cleanup can handle the onerror callback

Replacing Path.rglob with os.walk(..., onerror=...) and filtering only FileNotFoundError tolerates concurrently vanished lock directories while preserving recursive exact-root .rebar/run_snapshots discovery and propagating other filesystem errors

Scoping concrete Path factory through snapshot cleanup (conftest.py and snapshot.py _rmtree_writable) to the fixture's POSIX context eliminates ambiguous WindowsPath instantiation under active test monkeypatches

Original test scenario (test_mcp_run_workflow_is_async_and_pollable on Ubuntu/Python 3.11) reproducibly failed with FileNotFoundError at .ticket-write.lock.d; deterministic barrier oracle confirmed the lock-release / rglob-descent race as root cause, rejected async MCP and lock lifecycle as defects
